name: hologram
//peer: Whichever app is Jarvis brings its own copy of these; both of them depend on all nine directly. Skia is only a type import in the main entry, but the react entry calls into it, and the conversation entry calls into the ElevenLabs SDK (its client's `Conversation.startSession`, which must be the very copy `@elevenlabs/react-native` registers its session strategy on — `mobile/src/agent-audio-track.contract.spec.ts` checks it is) and, for the recorded greeting, LiveKit's audio session and hologram's own native player (expo) on a device, expo-audio in a browser. The native player is why this package has an expo-module.config.json: both apps autolink it.
//exports: Three entries, and the split matters: '.' is the design, the voice tracking, the ElevenLabs credentials and the conversation's framework-free parts, importing nothing from outside the package but types and the plain values of Skia's enums, so it runs headless in the tests, under CanvasKit in a browser, and in a client with no React at all. './react' is the view, which needs React, Reanimated and Skia for real. './conversation' needs React and the ElevenLabs SDK but deliberately not Skia, so a screen can hold a conversation before CanvasKit has loaded. './react/sample' is sample mode's clock-made voice, mood toast and frame-rate readout, Skia-free like './react/lifecycle' so a browser screen can import it before CanvasKit has loaded. './react/hologram-view' is for the browser build's lazy import() only — CanvasKit has to finish loading before anything Skia-backed is even imported. './assets/*' is the files themselves, for a bundler that takes a file as a URL rather than as Metro's asset id: the headset imports the greeting as `hologram/assets/greeting.mp3?url` and never reaches './conversation', whose greeting player is Metro's.
